title_en: DOJ subpoenas local election officials over claims of noncitizen voting in California
title_zh: 司法部就加州非公民投票的指控向当地选举官员发出传票
summary: The Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation in California as it continues its effort to prove that as many as 20,000 noncitizens are on the state’s voter rolls, a U.S. official confirmed to NBC News Thursday.
summary_zh: 司法部已在加州展开刑事调查，并继续努力证明多达 20,000 名非公民在
body_en: DOJ subpoenas local election officials over claims of noncitizen voting in California

The Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation in California as it continues its effort to prove that as many as 20,000 noncitizens are on the state’s voter rolls, a U.S. official confirmed to NBC News Thursday.

The official said that the DOJ has issued federal grand jury subpoenas to local election officials across the state, though it’s unclear how many subpoenas were sent out and exactly who received them.
The New York Times first reported the new subpoenas.

In response to an inquiry from NBC News on Thursday, the Justice Department declined to comment on “leaks about alleged grand jury subpoenas,” but added that federal courts have said voting unlawfully results in criminal exposure.

The U.S. official told NBC News that receiving a subpoena doesn’t mean that person is necessarily a target, just that they may have information relevant to the investigation. The official added that the Justice Department rarely subpoenas individuals it intends to charge with a crime.

The new subpoenas follow a federal judge’s ruling Wednesday to deny the Trump administration’s request to segregate 20,000 mail-in ballots from alleged noncitizens in California, calling into question the accuracy of the administration’s process to identify such individuals.
Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder and County Clerk Dean Logan touted the decision Thursday.

“At every step, the U.S. Department of Justice has taken a confrontational, adversarial approach. Election officials are acting in accordance with state and federal law,” Logan said in a statement, adding that “clear court rulings” by both the federal judge and an appeals court have confirmed that.

Last week, Justice Department officials sent letters to 57 of California’s 58 counties warning local election officials to cooperate with federal investigations into illegal voting or face investigations themselves.

Earlier this week the Justice Department expanded the efforts, sending similar letters to officials in Washington state and asking its secretary of state to review a list of 400 registrants whom the DOJ believes to be noncitizens. It also asked that the state sequester any ballots those individuals cast.

The Trump administration faced two legal setbacks on the efforts this week, after an appeals court denied its request Monday to block California from counting mail ballots from the alleged noncitizens and a federal judge Wednesday rejected its request to segregate those ballots.

The Trump administration has pressured state officials to assist in investigations of alleged voter fraud for months, having sued 30 states and the District of Columbia for refusing to hand over their voter registration list data.

While noncitizens can appear on voter rolls, it is a rare occurrence. Also, newly naturalized citizens are often mistakenly flagged as noncitizens, especially since there is no comprehensive list of U.S. citizens.
Election experts have argued that the Trump administration’s lawsuits rely on flimsy legal arguments , particularly as the DOJ does not have legal authority to intervene in election certification.

body_zh: 司法部就加州非公民投票的指控向当地选举官员发出传票
周四，一名美国官员向 NBC 新闻证实，司法部已在加州展开刑事调查，并继续努力证明该州选民名册上有多达 2 万名非公民。
该官员表示，司法部已向全州地方选举官员发出联邦大陪审团传票，但尚不清楚发出了多少张传票以及到底谁收到了传票。
《纽约时报》首先报道了新的传票。
在周四回应 NBC 新闻的询问时，司法部拒绝就“涉嫌大陪审团传票的泄露”发表评论，但补充说，联邦法院已表示非法投票会导致刑事曝光。
这位美国官员告诉 NBC 新闻，收到传票并不意味着该人一定是目标，只是表明他们可能掌握与调查相关的信息。该官员补充说，司法部很少传唤其打算指控犯罪的个人。
新传票是在联邦法官周三做出裁决后发出的，该裁决驳回了特朗普政府将 20,000 张邮寄选票与加州所谓的非公民分开的请求，这让人们对政府识别此类个人的程序的准确性提出了质疑。
洛杉矶县登记官和县书记员迪恩·洛根周四宣扬了这一决定。
洛根在一份声明中表示，“美国司法部的每一步都采取了对抗性的、对抗性的方式。选举官员是根据州和联邦法律行事的。”他补充说，联邦法官和上诉法院的“明确的法院裁决”已经证实了这一点。
上周，司法部官员致函加州 58 个县中的 57 个县，警告地方选举官员配合联邦对非法投票的调查，否则自己将面临调查。
本周早些时候，司法部加大了力度，向华盛顿州官员发出了类似的信件，并要求州务卿审查一份包含 400 名被司法部认为是非公民的登记者的名单。它还要求国家扣押这些人所投的任何选票。
特朗普政府本周的努力面临两项法律挫折，此前上诉法院周一驳回了其要求阻止加州清点所谓非公民邮寄选票的请求，而联邦法官周三则拒绝了其将这些选票分开的请求。
几个月来，特朗普政府一直向各州官员施压，要求他们协助调查所谓的选民欺诈行为，并起诉 30 个州和哥伦比亚特区拒绝交出选民登记名单数据。
虽然非公民可以出现在选民名册上，但这种情况很少见。此外，新入籍的公民经常被错误地标记为非公民，特别是因为没有完整的美国公民名单。
选举专家认为，特朗普政府的诉讼依赖于站不住脚的法律论据，特别是因为司法部没有干预选举认证的法律权力。

title_en: Alaska's all-important Senate race is roiled by a report on alleged spoiler candidate
title_zh: 阿拉斯加最重要的参议院竞选因一份涉嫌破坏候选人的报告而陷入混乱
summary: New reporting alleging Democratic efforts to prop up a spoiler candidate has roiled Alaska's all-important U.S. Senate race.
summary_zh: 新的报道称，民主党支持扰乱候选人的努力扰乱了阿拉斯加最重要的美国参议院竞选。
body_en: Dan Sullivans: Alaska Senate race roiled by spoiler reporting : NPR
Dan Sullivans: Alaska Senate race roiled by spoiler reporting New reporting alleging Democratic efforts to prop up a spoiler candidate has roiled Alaska's all-important U.S. Senate race.
Alaska's all-important Senate race is roiled by a report on alleged spoiler candidate
This combination photo shows Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, left, and another Senate candidate named Dan Sullivan. Mark Thiessen, Becky Bohrer/AP hide caption
Alaska's governor is ordering an investigation after a New York Times report on the state's toss-up U.S. Senate race , which could determine which party controls the chamber next year.

That story detailed efforts by Democratic campaign operatives to recruit what Republicans have long alleged is a spoiler candidate whose presence on the ballot could confuse voters and siphon support from the GOP incumbent. The two candidates share the name Dan Sullivan.

NPR hasn't independently confirmed the Times ' reporting, but it's roiled the Senate race just days before Election Day. Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman, is hoping to flip the seat for her party.
Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
The Times ' story is based on interviews and communications among Peltola's attorneys and advisers, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
Democrats have long denied involvement in the non-incumbent Sullivan's candidacy, and both the Peltola campaign and the DSCC reiterated those denials after the Times story published.

While campaigning Wednesday, Peltola called the story a distraction, according to Alaska Public Media , and the non-incumbent Sullivan did not respond to Alaska Public Media's requests for comment. He has previously said it was his decision to run for Senate.
Mary Peltola, a Democrat running for the U.S. Senate seat in Alaska, addresses supporters at an election watch party on Aug. 18 in Anchorage. Mark Thiessen/AP hide caption

"Mary Peltola and her campaign have spent months gaslighting Alaskans, denying a scheme they were running all along," Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sen. Sullivan, said in a statement . President Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election loss, called the Alaska findings "Voter Fraud at the Highest Level," in an online post .

Trump's Justice Department had already sought to intervene in the Senate race , asking a court last week to delay certification if the incumbent Sullivan loses by a small margin. The legal effort cited potential voter confusion stemming from the second Sullivan on the ballot.
Election law experts had broadly derided the DOJ's case as weak , in part because the Constitution grants states control over elections.
Judge denies the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots
The Sullivan candidacies had already been probed by state officials, but the Alaska Supreme Court ruled in June that the non-incumbent Sullivan could appear on the general election ballot.
Justice Department officials said Thursday the Times ' story expands its options for investigating the Senate race, and it filed an amended complaint citing the new reporting.

And in the wake of the Times story, Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy said Wednesday night that he is directing the state's Department of Public Safety to "investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted."
It's unclear what laws could have been violated.

丹·沙利文斯：扰乱报道扰乱了阿拉斯加参议员竞选 新的报道称，民主党支持扰乱候选人的努力扰乱了阿拉斯加最重要的美国参议院竞选。
阿拉斯加最重要的参议院竞选因一份涉嫌破坏候选人的报告而陷入混乱
这张组合照片显示的是阿拉斯加州共和党参议员丹·沙利文（左）和另一位名叫丹·沙利文的参议院候选人。马克·蒂森、贝基·博勒/美联社隐藏标题栏
《纽约时报》报道了阿拉斯加州的美国参议院竞选，这可能决定明年哪个政党控制参议院，之后阿拉斯加州州长下令进行调查。
这篇报道详细描述了民主党竞选人员为招募共和党人长期以来所谓的破坏性候选人所做的努力，该候选人出现在选票上可能会迷惑选民并夺走共和党现任议员的支持。两位候选人同名丹·沙利文。
NPR 尚未独立证实《纽约时报》的报道，但它在选举日前几天扰乱了参议院竞选。前国会女议员、民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉希望为她的政党翻转席位。
民主党仍准备取得进展，但民意调查显示了警告信号
《泰晤士报》的报道基于对佩尔托拉的律师和顾问以及民主党参议员竞选委员会高级助手的采访和交流。
民主党长期以来一直否认参与非现任沙利文的候选资格，佩尔托拉竞选团队和 DSCC 在《纽约时报》的报道发表后都重申了这些否认。
据阿拉斯加公共媒体报道，在周三的竞选活动中，佩尔托拉称这个故事分散了人们的注意力，非现任议员沙利文没有回应阿拉斯加公共媒体的置评请求。他此前曾表示，竞选参议员是他的决定。
8 月 18 日，竞选阿拉斯加美国参议院席位的民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉 (Mary Peltola) 在安克雷奇举行的选举观察派对上向支持者发表讲话。马克·蒂森/美联社隐藏标题栏
参议员沙利文的发言人内特·亚当斯在一份声明中说：“玛丽·佩尔托拉和她的竞选团队花了几个月的时间对阿拉斯加人进行煤气灯操纵，否认他们一直在实施的计划。”试图扭转 2020 年大选失利的特朗普总统在网上发帖称，阿拉斯加的调查结果是“最高级别的选民欺诈”。
特朗普的司法部已经寻求干预参议院竞选，并于上周要求法院在现任沙利文以微弱优势落败的情况下推迟认证。法律工作指出，选票上的第二个沙利文可能会让选民感到困惑。
选举法专家普遍嘲笑司法部的案件软弱无力，部分原因是宪法赋予各州对选举的控制权。
法官驳回司法部停止处理加州选票的提议
州官员已经对沙利文的候选资格进行了调查，但阿拉斯加州最高法院在六月裁定，非现任沙利文可以出现在大选选票上。
司法部官员周四表示，《纽约时报》的报道扩大了调查参议院竞选的选择，并援引新的报道提交了一份修改后的起诉书。
在《纽约时报》的报道之后，共和党州长迈克·邓利维 (Mike Dunleavy) 周三晚表示，他正在指示该州公共安全部“调查该计划是否违反了阿拉斯加州的法律，以及是否有必要提起刑事指控或民事诉讼。”
目前尚不清楚可能违反了哪些法律。

body_en: Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song | Canada
Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song
Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president

Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams , is Lake America.
In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump , accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores.

Trump signed an executive order in August directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America”, echoing his earlier, widely mocked decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico “the Gulf of America”.
Neil Young files second lawsuit against Trump for unauthorised use of Rockin’ in the Free World at rallies

The move further escalated a feud with Canada that has strained the longstanding alliance between the two countries. Trump’s decision has largely been met with derision in Canada, with some pointing out that the province of Ontario is named after the lake, not the other way around. Adams’s lyrics emphasise the roots of the name
The ‘lake of shining waters ’ is what the Iroquois called her
It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order.

Adams’s lyrics also suggest that Trump’s naming stunt was intended to deflect from the president’s other political problems, including the war in Iran and renewed scrutiny of the Jeffrey Epstein files.
So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram
While the Epstein files were getting traction

The song is part of what Adams described in a recent interview as a broader “love letter” to Canada: a songwriting project that began with an invitation from a film company to write about the Maritimes provinces of Canada and has since morphed into the upcoming album How’s It Goin’.
“After finishing the first song, I moved on to that one, and then moved on to another one, and then started thinking maybe I should just carry on with my theme,” he said.
As well as homages to Canadian heroes , the album also includes 51st State, released on 1 July – Canada Day – as another repudiation of Trump, in this case his efforts to annex Canada.
The first time he played the song in public was in the US.
“We weren’t sure how people were going to respond to it,” he said. “But we got a standing ovation every night for it. It made me think: perhaps, finally, the tide’s turning.”

像刀子一样切割：加拿大摇滚歌手布莱恩·亚当斯用新歌恶搞特朗普
音乐家用一张新专辑给加拿大写了一封“情书”——以及一些关于美国总统的尖锐评论
安大略湖是横跨美国和加拿大边境的广阔水域，几个世纪以来有过许多名字：圣路易斯湖、安大略湖、斯卡尼亚多里奥湖、卡塔拉基湖。但加拿大摇滚明星布莱恩·亚当斯 (Bryan Adams) 表示，它永远不会被称为“美洲湖”。
亚当斯在他的新歌《安大略湖》中将矛头指向了美国总统唐纳德·特朗普，指责他“破坏了”湖畔居民之间的和平。
特朗普于八月签署了一项行政命令，指示美国联邦机构将安大略湖重新命名为“美国湖”，这与他之前将墨西哥湾重新命名为“美洲湾”的广受嘲笑的决定相呼应。
尼尔·杨对特朗普提起第二次诉讼，指控他未经授权在集会上使用“自由世界摇滚”
此举进一步加剧了与加拿大的不和，使两国之间的长期联盟关系紧张。特朗普的决定在加拿大遭到了嘲笑，一些人指出安大略省是以该湖命名的，而不是相反。亚当斯的歌词强调了名字的根源
易洛魁人称她为“波光粼粼的湖水”
这是原住民的名字，而不是行政命令。
亚当斯的歌词还表明，特朗普的命名噱头是为了转移人们对总统其他政治问题的注意力，包括伊朗战争和对杰弗里·爱泼斯坦档案的重新审查。
就像婴儿从婴儿车里扔玩具一样
当爱泼斯坦的文件受到关注时
这首歌是亚当斯在最近的一次采访中描述的一封更广泛的写给加拿大的“情书”的一部分：一个歌曲创作项目，始于一家电影公司的邀请，写关于加拿大滨海省的内容，后来演变成即将发行的专辑《How’s It Goin’》。
“完成第一首歌后，我继续唱那首歌，然后又唱另一首歌，然后开始思考也许我应该继续我的主题，”他说。
除了向加拿大英雄致敬之外，这张专辑还收录了 7 月 1 日加拿大国庆日发行的《51st State》，作为对特朗普吞并加拿大努力的又一次否定。
他第一次在公开场合演奏这首歌是在美国。
“我们不确定人们会如何回应，”他说。 “但我们每天晚上都会为它起立鼓掌。这让我想到：也许潮流终于要转变了。”

body_en: Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race : NPR

Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.
Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race
Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.

President Trump is trying to preemptively block election results in Alaska if the Republican incumbent loses. But in that state, the big issue in the Senate race has been an emotional fight over fish. And that's because the salmon that have long sustained Indigenous people are not returning to some Western Alaska rivers. While people living in remote villages feel the loss of salmon most acutely, the issue could ultimately affect the balance of power thousands of miles away in Washington, D.C. Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin reports.
LIZ RUSKIN, BYLINE: Evon Waska lives at the water's edge, where he says his parents settled when they gave up their nomadic life.
EVON WASKA: Well, this is my smokehouse, and this is where we make smoke, right?

RUSKIN: Waska's drying racks should be filled with salmon, but they're empty. Most years now, too few salmon return from the Bering Sea to his river, the Kuskokwim. To conserve fish, government agencies often close the river to fishing, even to those like Waska who fish to feed their families. Waska blames trawlers, industrial fishing boats miles offshore.
WASKA: They don't close the trawlers. They close me and my people first.

RUSKIN: Waska is up against a $1 billion industry, much of it based in Seattle. Picture a sock-shaped net that's a quarter mile long with an opening as wide as a football field. That's what trawlers tow to catch pollock. The white fish is served to you as imitation crab in McDonald's Filet-O-Fish. But also scooped up in those nets are prized king salmon and other fish. They're caught by accident and wasted, a problem known as bycatch. Alaskans are increasingly angry about it. Now, in a year where Alaska could decide the balance of power in the U.S. Senate, fish are all over political ads here.

UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #1: Senator Sullivan is championing legislation to reduce bycatch and strengthen Alaska's fisheries. Call Senator Dan Sullivan. Thank him and tell him to keep fighting for Alaska fishermen.
UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #2: Dan Sullivan is taking big money from out-of-state corporate trawlers.
UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #3: Mary Peltola tells a lot of fish tales to get votes.
RUSKIN: Republican Senator Dan Sullivan has been an ally of the pollock industry. But this year, he's touting a new bill.
DAN SULLIVAN: It's the most comprehensive bycatch legislation ever to reduce bycatch, protect seafloor habitat.

RUSKIN: Democratic Senate challenger Mary Peltola is Indigenous, from the Kuskokwim. She says she'd ban factory trawlers, the largest of the pollock fleet. She calls Sullivan's bill an election year ploy.
MARY PELTOLA: Dan Sullivan reeled in over $300,000 from trawlers and waited until the 11th hour for a half-hearted and half-baked solution.
RUSKIN: Heather Mann (ph) leads a trawlers association. She says scapegoating the pollock fishery won't help western Alaska.
HEATHER MANN: Even if you were to eliminate pollock, the chances of salmon runs being restored, what the science shows us is it would have a minimal impact.
body_zh: 钓鱼是阿拉斯加激烈的美国参议院竞选中的一个关键问题：NPR
渔业是阿拉斯加紧张的美国参议员竞选中的一个关键问题阿拉斯加的美国参议员竞选卷入了一场关于鱼类的激烈斗争。该州许多人依靠鲑鱼养家糊口，但这些鱼和其他鱼越来越难找到。
渔业是阿拉斯加激烈的美国参议院竞选中的一个关键问题
阿拉斯加州的美国参议员竞选卷入了一场围绕鱼类的激烈斗争。该州许多人依靠鲑鱼养家糊口，但这些鱼和其他鱼越来越难找到。
如果共和党现任总统输了，特朗普总统正试图先发制人地阻止阿拉斯加的选举结果。但在那个州，参议院竞选中的大问题是围绕鱼的激烈争论。这是因为长期供养原住民的鲑鱼没有返回阿拉斯加西部的一些河流。据阿拉斯加公共媒体莉兹·罗斯金报道，虽然生活在偏远村庄的人们对鲑鱼的减少感受最深，但这个问题最终可能会影响千里之外的华盛顿特区的权力平衡。
莉兹·拉斯金连线：埃文·瓦斯卡住在水边，他说他的父母放弃游牧生活后定居在那里。
EVON WASKA：嗯，这是我的烟房，这是我们制作烟的地方，对吗？
拉斯金：瓦斯卡的晾衣架上应该装满了鲑鱼，但它们是空的。现在大多数年份，从白令海返回库斯科奎姆河的鲑鱼太少了。为了保护鱼类，政府机构经常禁止在这条河上捕鱼，甚至禁止像瓦斯卡这样靠捕鱼养家糊口的人。瓦斯卡将此归咎于拖网渔船和离岸数英里的工业渔船。
WASKA：他们不会关闭拖网渔船。他们首先关闭了我和我的人民。

拉斯金：瓦斯卡面临着一个价值 10 亿美元的行业，其中大部分位于西雅图。想象一张袜子形状的网，四分之一英里长，开口与足球场一样宽。这就是拖网渔船用来捕捞狭鳕的东西。麦当劳的 Filet-O-Fish 中的白鱼是仿螃蟹。但这些网中还捕获了珍贵的帝王鲑和其他鱼类。它们被意外捕获并被浪费，这个问题被称为兼捕。阿拉斯加人对此越来越愤怒。现在，在阿拉斯加可能决定美国参议院权力平衡的一年里，这里的政治广告上到处都是鱼。
身份不明的旁白 #1：沙利文参议员正在倡导立法，以减少兼捕并加强阿拉斯加的渔业。致电参议员丹·沙利文。感谢他并告诉他继续为阿拉斯加渔民而战。
身份不明的旁白 #2：丹·沙利文从州外企业拖网渔船上赚了大笔钱。
身份不明的叙述者#3：玛丽·佩尔托拉讲了很多鱼的故事来获得选票。
罗斯金：共和党参议员丹·沙利文一直是狭鳕产业的盟友。但今年，他提出了一项新法案。
丹·沙利文：这是有史以来最全面的兼捕立法，旨在减少兼捕、保护海底栖息地。
拉斯金：民主党参议院挑战者玛丽·佩尔托拉 (Mary Peltola) 是来自库斯科奎姆 (Kuskokwim) 的原住民。她说她将禁止工厂拖网渔船，这是最大的狭鳕船队。她称沙利文的法案是选举年的策略。
玛丽·佩尔托拉：丹·沙利文从拖网渔船上筹集了超过 30 万美元，直到第 11 个小时才得到一个半心半意、半生不熟的解决方案。
拉斯金：希瑟·曼（博士）领导着一个拖网渔船协会。她说，将狭鳕渔业作为替罪羊对阿拉斯加西部没有帮助。
希瑟·曼：即使消灭了狭鳕，鲑鱼洄游的机会得以恢复，科学向我们表明，影响也很小。

body_en: Ex-congresswoman is connecting with young people and Native voters with promise to expand the social safety net

The road to Isleta Pueblo, a Native American tribal community just 20 minutes south of downtown Albuquerque, New Mexico , is peppered with campaign signs. Among the many names of candidates running in next week’s midterm elections and tribal elections later in November, there’s one that is poised to make history.

Deb Haaland is set to become the first Native American female governor in the US when voters cast their ballots on 3 November. Recent polling shows her with a comfortable lead over her opponent, Republican Gregg Hull, a businessman and the longtime mayor of the city of Rio Rancho. Her bid for office also signals the growing power of the Democratic party in the state, where Democrats control the legislature, hold all top offices and have enacted progressive policies, such as universal childcare , that have been heralded across the country.
body_zh: 前女议员正在与年轻人和原住民选民联系，承诺扩大社会安全网
通往伊斯莱塔普韦布洛 (Isleta Pueblo) 的道路上布满了竞选标语。伊斯莱塔普韦布洛是一个美洲原住民部落社区，距离新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基市中心以南仅 20 分钟路程。在参加下周中期选举和 11 月晚些时候部落选举的众多候选人中，有一位即将创造历史。
11 月 3 日选民投票时，黛布·哈兰德将成为美国第一位美洲原住民女州长。最近的民意调查显示，她轻松领先于对手、共和党人格雷格·赫尔（Gregg Hull），后者是一位商人，也是里奥兰乔市的长期市长。她的竞选也标志着民主党在该州的权力不断增强，民主党控制着立法机构，担任所有高级职位，并制定了进步政策，例如全民儿童保育，这些政策在全国范围内广受好评。

Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff is likely to win the Senate race, while Georgia's governor race remains uncertain. Millions have already cast their votes early, and Fowler says data show increased turnout among Latino and young voters in Democratic areas, as well as among non-supervoters, who typically don't participate in primaries. The trend creates some uncertainty around what the final electorate will look like, and indicates that Republicans will have to rely on a large Election Day turnout to stay competitive, Fowler says.

➡️ A federal judge has denied the Department of Justice's emergency request to halt the processing of ballots for 20,000 individuals it identified as "likely" noncitizens. The department filed a notice that it is appealing the decision .
➡️ Across the U.S., voters will see 145 statewide ballot measures on the November ballot, according to Ballotpedia. Key themes include abortion, LGBTQ+ rights, taxes, and voting .

➡️ The NPR App has all of NPR's election coverage in one place — from the biggest stories across the country, to the issues that matter close to home. Browse headlines, playlists, podcast episodes, videos and more, all on the 2026 Election tab .

Americans will receive a final reading on the country's gross domestic product and the state of inflation today before next week's midterm election. The report will show whether the economy grew faster in the summer compared to spring. Economists expect GDP to be higher, but some say the growth feels delicate.

🎧 The tech industry's continued investment in artificial intelligence and consumer spending are driving the GDP , NPR's Stephan Bisaha says. But economist Mark Zandi tells him it's a "very, very fragile growth." Zandi blames inflation for this sense of fragility. Consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, and prices are outpacing wage growth. After keeping interest rates steady yesterday, the Fed will be paying close attention to today's inflation reading from the Commerce Department.

Israel's election is in a deadlock. More than 90% of the votes have been counted, and no candidate has a clear path to forming a coalition. Parties need 61 seats in parliament for a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies have secured 53 seats, while his top rival Gadi Eisenkot and his allies have garnered 48.

🎧 NPR's Daniel Estrin says there are several options for breaking the impasse. Eisenkot's camp could win by partnering with Arab-led parties, which recently secured a record 19 seats in parliament, NPR's Daniel Estrin says. But this partnership seems unlikely due to the political risks . Estrin says Arab political leaders in Israel have been demonized. Israel could hold repeat elections, but Eisenkot doesn't want that because the opposition would have a hard time getting votes a second time. Estrin says Eisenkot will be under pressure to enter a unity government with Netanyahu, especially if Israel launches a new war with Iran.

A lawsuit filed yesterday against the Department of Education alleges that the Trump administration is illegally refusing to follow the rules of a program known as "closed school discharge." For more than three decades, federal law has required the U.S. Secretary of Education to cancel debts for qualified borrowers when their schools close unexpectedly. Student Defense, a nonprofit borrower advocacy group, filed the suit on behalf of potentially thousands of borrowers. The Education Department told NPR it stands by its implementation of the program.

Bernie Taupin is Elton John's lyricist on nearly every album. Now, for the first time in 40 years, he's stepping into the spotlight. His new album, The Sea Has No Mercy , features a collection of songs entirely written and sung by him. Taupin admits that until recently, he hadn't considered writing for himself, but now he's ready to share his own musical voice. He tells Morning Edition 's A Martínez that more so than a songwriter and a lyricist, Taupin thinks of himself as a storyteller. Listen to snippets of the album and hear about how Taupin has been able to keep his and John's relationship so strong.

Medicare's open enrollment window runs through Dec. 7. More than half of Americans in Medicare choose a Medicare Advantage plan, which is run by private insurers instead of the federal government. Medicare Advantage is popular because it covers dental and vision, often with lower premiums than traditional Medicare. But private carriers can pick and choose where it's offered, and withdraw from unprofitable communities. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump handed out candy to hundreds of costumed kids outside the White House residence at Thursday's annual Halloween celebration.

A line of visitors stretched down the driveway while the Trumps, who were not wearing costumes, passed out jumbo candy bars. Trump chatted with parents and posed for photos alongside children dressed as figures including Barbie, Tigger, Batman and several founding fathers.
The White House entrance was bedecked with pumpkins, ivy and a giant faux moon for the occasion, while a military performed Halloween classics.
Midway through, Trump paused to take in a low flyover of his Qatari Air Force One jet.

body_en: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner over what official says were leaks to media - CBS News
Washington — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, several sources confirmed to CBS News late Wednesday.

A Pentagon official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was accused of misconduct for allegedly leaking classified information related to the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine war .
Sylvia failed three polygraph tests about sharing classified information with the press, the official said, adding that the case has been referred to the Department of Justice.
Two other Pentagon sources confirmed to CBS News that the firing was related to the polygraph tests, but said those accusations are not true.

Hegseth has made rooting out leakers at the Pentagon a priority, with sources telling CBS News last month that high-ranking military officials were subject to polygraph tests. Three staffers from his office were escorted out last year amid a leak investigation, but the Pentagon never released the results of any investigation.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell did not name Sylvia by name in a statement on social media , but said that "following an extensive Air Force OSI investigation, the Department took necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information."

"To protect the integrity of the investigation, no further comment will be made regarding the individual or the circumstances of this action," Parnell continued. "This matter, along with others, have been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action. Classified information is not personal property. Leaking it for personal, political or professional gain is a betrayal of the trust placed in those responsible for keeping it. Our commitment was not an empty promise. We vowed to find you, and we meant it."
Sylvia's firing comes as President Trump weighs resuming strikes against Iran after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, and was coordinating the Iran battle plan. Sylvia is the second general during Hegseth's tenure to be removed from what is known as a "J5" post, which is the lead on how the Iran war affects long-term planning. Sylvia's predecessor, Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee, was forced to retire in October 2025.
The firing was reported earlier by The Atlantic .
After initially issuing a statement extending "the deepest gratitude" for Slyvia's 32 years of service, a spokesperson for the Joint Staff retracted the statement and issued a new one.

"Upon further review, we determined that the statement did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances," the spokesperson said. "Out of respect for the servicemember and the ongoing personnel process we will not comment further."

Sylvia is a former commander of the 101st Airborne Division with multiple deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq, earned a Bronze Star for Valor. He was a Purple Heart recipient after being wounded in battle in that gunfight with the Taliban, and he had a storied combat career that spanned 32 years.

华盛顿——周三晚间，几位消息人士向哥伦比亚广播公司新闻证实，国防部长皮特·赫格斯已解雇五角大楼最高军事规划师。
一位因讨论敏感人事问题而要求匿名的五角大楼官员表示，陆军中将布雷特·西尔维娅因涉嫌泄露与伊朗战争和俄罗斯-乌克兰战争有关的机密信息而被指控行为不当。
这位官员表示，西尔维娅未能通过三项有关与媒体分享机密信息的测谎仪测试，并补充说此案已移交给司法部。
五角大楼的另外两名消息人士向哥伦比亚广播公司新闻证实，此次解雇与测谎仪测试有关，但表示这些指控并不属实。
赫格斯已将铲除五角大楼的泄密者作为首要任务，上个月有消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，高级军事官员接受了测谎仪测试。去年，在一次泄密调查中，他办公室的三名工作人员被护送出境，但五角大楼从未公布任何调查结果。
五角大楼发言人肖恩·帕内尔在社交媒体上的一份声明中没有点名西尔维娅，但表示“在进行广泛的空军现场视察调查后，国防部采取了必要的人事行动来保护敏感信息。”
帕内尔继续说道：“为了保护调查的完整性，我们不会对此次行动的个人或情况发表进一步的评论。” “这件事以及其他问题已被提交给司法部，以便采取进一步的法律行动。机密信息不是个人财产。为了个人、政治或职业利益而泄露这些信息是对负责保管这些信息的人的信任的背叛。我们的承诺不是空洞的承诺。我们发誓要找到你，我们是认真的。”
西尔维娅被解雇之际，特朗普总统正在考虑在 11 月 3 日中期选举后恢复对伊朗的打击。
西尔维娅被免去联合参谋部战略、计划和政策负责人的职务，并负责协调伊朗作战计划。西尔维娅是赫格塞斯任期内第二位被解除“J5”职位的将军，该职位是伊朗战争如何影响长期规划的主要负责人。西尔维娅的前任约瑟夫·麦吉中将被迫于 2025 年 10 月退休。
《大西洋月刊》早些时候报道了此次解雇事件。
联合参谋部发言人最初发表声明对斯利维亚 32 年的服役表示“最深切的谢意”，但随后撤回了该声明并发表了新声明。
发言人表示：“经过进一步审查，我们确定该声明未能恰当反映全部情况。” “出于对军人和正在进行的人事流程的尊重，我们不会进一步发表评论。”
西尔维娅是第 101 空降师的前指挥官，曾多次部署到阿富汗和伊拉克，因勇敢而获得铜星勋章。他在与塔利班的枪战中受伤后获得了紫心勋章，并拥有长达 32 年的传奇战斗生涯。

body_en: The 2026 midterms already face a messy pileup of lawsuits and ballot battles, raising fears about election confidence before voters even finish casting ballots .

Why it matters: Election challenges aren't unusual, but as the Trump administration continues to make false claims about widespread voter fraud, officials are juggling fights over voter lists, mail-ballot rules and election certification challenges.

What they're saying: "The types of challenges that we are seeing pre-election, this close to election day, are very unusual, and mostly because they are coming from the federal government," Jonathan Diaz of the Campaign Legal Center told Axios.
"These lawsuits are frivolous," Diaz said, adding they could "create doubt in the minds of the public about the legitimacy of the election process."
The other side: The White House referred Axios to comments President Trump made to the media.
The Department of Justice did not respond to Axios' request for comment.
Here's some of the ways chaos and uncertainty have shaped the 2026 midterms
In the Golden State, the Trump administration asked state election officials to set aside ballots from roughly 20,000 registered voters whom the DOJ suspects are noncitizens.
A federal judge rejected that push Wednesday night, warning that the administration lacked sufficient evidence to justify potentially disenfranchising eligible voters.
The judge noted that the DOJ had made similar claims in neighboring Nevada, where election officials determined that 185 voters the DOJ had flagged as noncitizens were actually U.S. citizens.
Diaz told Axios that, from his perspective as a voting-rights advocate, the California battle is "not a real lawsuit. It's a political press release that they just happened to submit to the court."
The other side: The White House directed questions about the ruling to remarks Trump made Thursday, in which he said "California is very corrupt," and the state's elections are "extremely corrupt."
On Monday, the two U.S. attorneys' offices in Washington state asked the state to set aside ballots from more than 400 people they allege were illegally registered to vote.
The letter mirrors similar demands sent to California before the Trump administration sued.
Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs fired back Wednesday, tearing into the U.S. attorneys for making the request so close to Election Day and calling the timing "profoundly disappointing."
Hobbs said a preliminary investigation confirmed that the federal list includes U.S. citizens and is unreliable. He asked prosecutors to provide individualized proof of ineligibility.
Nearly 4,000 mail-in ballots, or about 6%, processed in North Carolina through Oct. 24 have been flagged for problems that, if not fixed, could invalidate voters' choices.
Time is running out for those voters to address the issues, and hundreds have yet to respond to notifications about their ballots.

The rejections appear to stem in part from new guidance issued by the GOP-controlled state Board of Elections requiring the inner ballot envelope to be sealed, even if the outer envelope is already sealed.
In Alaska's Senate race , two men named Dan Sullivan are on the ballot, Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan.
body_zh: 2026 年中期选举已经面临一系列混乱的诉讼和选票战，选民甚至在完成投票之前就引发了对选举信心的担忧。
重要性：选举挑战并不罕见，但随着特朗普政府继续对普遍存在的选民欺诈做出虚假声明，官员们正在处理选民名单、邮寄投票规则和选举认证挑战等问题。
他们的说法：“我们在临近选举日的选举前看到的挑战类型非常不寻常，主要是因为它们来自联邦政府，”竞选法律中心的乔纳森·迪亚兹 (Jonathan Diaz) 告诉 Axios。
迪亚兹说：“这些诉讼毫无意义。”他补充说，它们可能“让公众对选举过程的合法性产生怀疑”。
另一方：白宫将 Axios 转介给特朗普总统向媒体发表的评论。
司法部没有回应 Axios 的置评请求。
以下是混乱和不确定性影响 2026 年中期选举的一些方式
在金州，特朗普政府要求州选举官员暂缓大约 20,000 名司法部怀疑为非公民的登记选民的选票。
周三晚上，一名联邦法官驳回了这一提议，警告称政府缺乏足够的证据来证明可能剥夺合格选民选举权的合理性。
法官指出，司法部在邻近的内华达州也提出了类似的主张，该州选举官员确定，司法部标记为非公民的 185 名选民实际上是美国公民。
迪亚兹告诉 Axios，从他作为投票权倡导者的角度来看，加州之争“不是真正的诉讼。这是他们只是碰巧向法院提交的政治新闻稿。”
另一面：白宫将有关裁决的质疑指向特朗普周四的言论，他在言论中表示“加州非常腐败”，该州的选举“极其腐败”。
周一，华盛顿州的两家美国检察官办公室要求该州搁置 400 多名他们声称非法登记投票的人的选票。
这封信反映了特朗普政府起诉之前向加州发出的类似要求。
华盛顿国务卿史蒂夫·霍布斯周三予以回击，猛烈抨击美国检察官在临近选举日之际提出这一要求，并称时机“非常令人失望”。
霍布斯表示，初步调查证实，联邦名单中包括美国公民，并不可靠。他要求检察官提供个人不合格证明。
截至 10 月 24 日，北卡罗来纳州处理的近 4,000 张邮寄选票（约占 6%）已被标记为存在问题，如果不解决这些问题，可能会使选民的选择无效。
这些选民解决这些问题的时间已经不多了，数百人尚未回复有关选票的通知。
拒绝的部分原因似乎是共和党控制的州选举委员会发布的新指南，要求密封内选票信封，即使外信封已经密封。
在阿拉斯加参议员竞选中，有两名名叫丹·沙利文的男子参加了投票，即参议员丹·沙利文和退休教师丹·沙利文。

title_en: El-Sayed’s allies fear Trump’s anti-Muslim attacks are reaching undecided voters
title_zh: 赛义德的盟友担心特朗普的反穆斯林攻击正在影响尚未做出决定的选民
summary: After Trump called him a “jihadist,” Abdul El-Sayed brushed off the “desperate, bad faith attacks”
summary_zh: 在特朗普称他为“圣战分子”后，阿卜杜勒·赛义德对“绝望的、恶意的攻击”不予理睬。
body_en: DEARBORN, MICHIGAN — “A threat to America.” “Radical ideology.” “A jihadist.”

President Donald Trump and Republicans are ratcheting up their efforts to brand Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan-born Muslim whose parents emigrated from Egypt, as an “extremist” in the final days of the state’s critical Senate race.

It has sparked concern among some El-Sayed supporters, who fear the deluge of attacks could break through to some undecided voters. It has infuriated some of the president’s one-time Muslim and Arab allies in the state with the largest concentration of Arab Americans in the country, who view the comments as Islamophobic and racist. And it has caused some of them to lose hope in Republicans.

“You turned off a lot of people. Even people that were working to get Trump elected and get people to vote Republican here have flipped. We did all this work for them to turn around and use us as enemies, to be able just to win an election,” said Hassan Nehme, a GOP statehouse candidate and former Michigan Republican Party vice chair who helped lead Arab American outreach for the GOP in 2024. He is undecided in how he’ll vote in this year’s Senate race. “It's to the point [where] I'm like, why am I even fighting to be in this party?”
Republicans’ increasingly incendiary rhetoric in the crucial Senate race is overshadowing the close of an already polarizing election.

“Michigan is a battleground. That’s the truth. And racism is real,” Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud, a Democrat in an Arab-majority city who is backing El-Sayed , said in an interview at his office Tuesday. “If you have folks who refuse to vote for somebody because of the direction in which they pray, it most certainly has an impact.”
Hammoud believes most voters will see past it. But Republicans are bearing down.

Trump, who has repeatedly mocked and mispronounced El-Sayed’s name, labeled him a “jihadist” during a rally for GOP nominee Mike Rogers in Port Huron this past Sunday and said he would “be unable to get a seat on an airplane.”

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., in a campaign event with Rogers in Grand Rapids on Monday, claimed the world’s 500 million Arabs no longer produce award-winning science or literature and instead create “stagnant societies that do two things — hatred and war and victimization.”
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), while campaigning for Rogers in Michigan on Wednesday, called El-Sayed a “jihadist leprechaun.”

Ads from Rogers’ campaign and allied GOP groups attacking El-Sayed in this vein run in rotation across Michigan television. Senate Leadership Fund , the top GOP Senate super PAC, says El-Sayed gets “dirty money” from an “Islamic extremist group” that is “tied to Hamas.” Rogers, in a direct-to-camera clip , calls El-Sayed “a threat to America.”
Bishara Bahbah, an Arizona resident who founded Arab Americans for Trump and helped facilitate Trump’s 2024 outreach to Michigan’s Arab community, said Trump’s Sunday comments cross “a red line.”
“The only consequence that I can see from these comments is a complete reversal of the support in Michigan and other states where Arabs and Muslims vote, toward the Democratic Party.”

Rogers has been more specific in how he’s gone after his opponent. He has attacked El-Sayed for taking campaign donations from donors affiliated with the Council on American-Islamic Relations , a Muslim advocacy group, which Republicans have long attacked as a terrorist group even though the U.S. government has not designated it as such. He’s alleged ties between El-Sayed’s family and the Muslim Brotherhood, in part through El-Sayed’s father-in-law’s involvement with CAIR and the Islamic Society of North America , another Muslim group . El-Sayed’s campaign referred to past statements from both CAIR and ISNA denying affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. Rogers has also referenced El-Sayed’s mother’s work for a charity that the Bush administration classified as a supporter of terrorist groups , as reported by The New York Times.

El-Sayed has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood and said his family has “no” ties to it . El-Sayed’s parents separated when he was three years old, and he says he was raised by his father and stepmother. His campaign responded to Trump’s rally in a statement saying while Trump and Rogers “lie and resort to desperate, bad faith attacks, Abdul remains laser focused on his plans to bring down costs and stand up to the chaos and corruption in Washington.”

“I’m not worried,” El-Sayed told reporters at a Detroit union hall on Monday, “because just like I did 18 months ago when I kicked off this campaign, I am taking a bet on the bigness of Michiganders.”
And President Barack Obama, in a rally with El-Sayed in Detroit on Saturday, said: “This stuff didn’t work on me, not in Michigan. It’s not going to work on Abdul.”
James Tate, president of the Detroit City Council noted that El-Sayed “can’t defend himself in every household."

El-Sayed’s campaign and his allies are fighting back by knocking on doors and hitting the airwaves, a sign they’re cognizant the attacks could have an impact. One El-Sayed ad features his white step-grandparents responding to some of Trump’s attacks. “Communist? We’re Presbyterian!" his grandparents say in the spot .
El-Sayed cut another ad featuring images of a menorah and of him praying with Black parishioners.
body_zh: 密歇根州迪尔伯恩——“对美国的威胁。” “激进的意识形态。” “一个圣战分子。”
在该州关键的参议院竞选的最后几天，唐纳德·特朗普总统和共和党人正在加紧努力，将民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德（Abdul El-Sayed）贴上“极端分子”的标签。阿卜杜勒·赛义德是一位出生于密歇根州的穆斯林，其父母是从埃及移民的。
这引起了一些赛义德支持者的担忧，他们担心大量袭击可能会波及一些犹豫不决的选民。这激怒了总统在该国阿拉伯裔美国人最集中的州的一些曾经的穆斯林和阿拉伯盟友，他们认为这些言论是仇视伊斯兰和种族主义的。这导致他们中的一些人对共和党失去了希望。

“你让很多人失去了兴趣。即使是那些努力让特朗普当选、让人们在这里投票给共和党的人也变得反常了。我们做了所有这些工作，就是为了让他们转身，把我们当作敌人，以便能够赢得选举。”共和党州议会候选人、前密歇根州共和党副主席哈桑·内梅(Hassan Nehme)说，他曾帮助领导阿拉伯裔美国人在2024年为共和党做宣传。他尚未决定在今年的参议院竞选中如何投票。 “到了这个地步，我就想，为什么我要为加入这个派对而奋斗呢？”
共和党人在关键的参议院竞选中日益煽动的言论给本已两极分化的选举的结束蒙上了阴影。
“密歇根州是一个战场。这是事实。种族主义是真实存在的，”迪尔伯恩市市长阿卜杜拉·哈穆德（Abdullah Hammoud）周二在办公室接受采访时表示，他是一个阿拉伯人占多数的城市的民主党人，支持埃尔-赛义德。 “如果有人因为祈祷的方向而拒绝投票给某人，那肯定会产生影响。”
哈穆德相信大多数选民都会看到这一点。但共和党人正在采取行动。
特朗普曾多次嘲笑和误读埃尔·赛义德的名字，上周日在休伦港举行的共和党候选人迈克·罗杰斯集会上，他将埃尔·赛义德称为“圣战分子”，并表示他将“无法在飞机上找到座位”。
卫生与公共服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 周一在大急流城与罗杰斯一起参加竞选活动，声称世界上 5 亿阿拉伯人不再创造屡获殊荣的科学或文学，而是创造“停滞的社会，做两件事——仇恨、战争和受害”。
参议员特德·克鲁兹（德克萨斯州共和党人）周三在密歇根州为罗杰斯竞选时称埃尔·赛义德为“圣战妖精”。
罗杰斯竞选团队和共和党盟友团体以这种方式攻击埃尔赛义德的广告在密歇根电视台轮流播放。共和党最高参议院超级政治行动委员会参议院领导基金表示，埃尔赛义德从“与哈马斯有联系”的“伊斯兰极端组织”那里获得了“黑钱”。罗杰斯在一个直接镜头剪辑中称埃尔赛义德“对美国构成威胁”。
亚利桑那州居民比沙拉·巴巴 (Bishara Bahbah) 为特朗普创立了阿拉伯裔美国人组织，并帮助促进特朗普 2024 年与密歇根州阿拉伯社区的接触，他表示特朗普周日的言论跨越了“红线”。
“我从这些评论中看到的唯一后果是密歇根州和其他阿拉伯人和穆斯林投票的州对民主党的支持完全逆转。”

罗杰斯更具体地阐述了他如何追击对手。他攻击埃尔赛义德从隶属于美国伊斯兰关系委员会的捐助者那里获取竞选捐款，该委员会是一个穆斯林倡导组织，共和党人长期以来一直将其攻击为恐怖组织，尽管美国政府尚未将其列为恐怖组织。他声称，赛义德家族与穆斯林兄弟会之间存在联系，部分原因是赛义德的岳父参与 CAIR 和另一个穆斯林组织北美伊斯兰协会。赛义德的竞选活动提到了 CAIR 和 ISNA 过去否认与穆斯林兄弟会有联系的声明。据《纽约时报》报道，罗杰斯还提到了埃尔赛义德母亲为一家慈善机构所做的工作，该慈善机构被布什政府列为恐怖组织的支持者。
埃尔-赛义德否认穆斯林兄弟会的存在，并表示他的家人与该组织“没有”任何关系。埃尔-赛义德的父母在他三岁时就分居了，他说他是由父亲和继母抚养长大的。他的竞选团队在一份声明中回应特朗普的集会，称虽然特朗普和罗杰斯“撒谎并诉诸绝望的恶意攻击，但阿卜杜勒仍然专注于降低成本并对抗华盛顿的混乱和腐败的计划。”
“我并不担心，”埃尔-赛义德周一在底特律工会大厅对记者说，“因为就像我 18 个月前开始竞选时所做的那样，我把赌注押在了密歇根人的伟大上。”
周六，美国总统巴拉克·奥巴马 (Barack Obama) 在底特律与埃尔·赛义德 (El-Sayed) 举行的集会上表示：“这些东西对我不起作用，在密歇根州也不起作用。它对阿卜杜勒也不起作用。”
底特律市议会主席詹姆斯·泰特指出，埃尔·赛义德“无法在每个家庭中为自己辩护”。
埃尔-赛义德的竞选团队和他的盟友正在通过挨家挨户敲门和广播进行反击，这表明他们意识到这些袭击可能会产生影响。埃尔赛义德的一则广告中，他的白人继祖父母对特朗普的一些攻击做出了回应。 “共产主义？我们是长老会！”他的爷爷奶奶当场说道。
埃尔-赛义德还制作了另一则广告，其中有烛台的图像以及他与黑人教区居民一起祈祷的图像。

title_en: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
title_zh: 这些是 11 月 3 日举行的 2026 年中期选举中值得关注的众议院竞选
summary: An NPR analysis finds 70 House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each investing more than six figures in advertising during the final few days of the election, including in deep red areas.
summary_zh: NPR 的一项分析发现，在最后几年里，民主党和共和党在 70 个众议院选区的广告投入均超过六位数
body_en: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
A worker holds I Voted Today stickers during early voting on October 14, 2026 in Des Moines, Iowa. Charlie Neibergall/Getty Images hide caption
In the final week of the 2026 midterm election, ad spending data suggests the core battle is less about stopping a Democratic wave in the House, and more about figuring out how high it crests.
An NPR analysis finds the final competitive House landscape is expansive, including 70 districts where both parties are investing at least six figures per district into their final days of messaging.

That includes more than $10 million each in toss up districts in Michigan, North Carolina, New York and Florida; seven figure ad buys in deep-red communities across Tennessee, Oklahoma and Arkansas and last-minute resources to districts where gerrymandering by Republicans could backfire.
In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map

In a midterm environment that disfavors the party in power, Republicans' narrow 218-214 seat advantage in the House appears all but certain to give way to Democratic control. The latest ratings from the Cook Political Report finds Democrats favored in 220 seats, 17 listed as "toss-ups" and another 30 that are potentially competitive but lean toward the GOP.

Most of the seats that saw narrow margins in the 2024 presidential election cycle have shifted the way of the Democrats, especially in the 10 districts that voted for one party's presidential candidate and the other party's House nominee.
That includes seats held by Democratic Reps. Adam Gray (CA-13), Nellie Pou (NJ-09) and Marie Gluesenkamp-Perez (WA-03) and retiring Republican Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02).
All four of those districts have seen Republicans slash ad reservations in recent weeks, according to AdImpact data.

The latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds Democrats have a 10-point advantage among registered voters and 8 points with likely voters on the generic congressional ballot. That means a far broader number of seats are competitive on paper, before accounting for candidate quality or outside spending.

Cost of living remains the top concern for voters, as rising gas prices, tariffs and the ongoing war in Iran factor into economic woes for many Americans. At the same time, a record number of Congressional retirement announcements has been amplified by an anti-incumbency streak in primary elections.

A wave of mid-decade redistricting after a Supreme Court decision that further rolled back part of the Voting Rights Act further scrambled the map, as Republicans shifted boundary lines to add more conservative voters into districts held by Democratic Reps. Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Don Davis (NC-01), Shomari Figures (AL-02) and Darren Soto (FL-09).

(Democrats did the same in California for the districts currently held by Republican Reps. James Gallagher (CA-01), David Valadao (CA-22), Ken Calvert (CA-41), Darrell Issa (CA-48) and independent Kevin Kiley (CA-06)).
Only Figures and Soto are in districts that are rated as currently favoring Republicans.
A tumultuous congressional primary season closes with record departures and defeats

As millions of voters have already cast their ballots in the midterms, there are dozens of races Democrats and Republicans consider worthy of heavy investment in the final hours to help shape the outcome.

Most expensive among them: Michigan's 7th District and North Carolina's 1st District —each with more than $12 million in spending planned; Florida's 14th, 22nd and 25th Districts; New York's 17th District; Iowa's 2nd and 3rd Districts and a slew of other races that either favor Democrats or are considered toss ups.

They include seats redrawn by Republicans this year to minimize Democratic voting power, like Alabama's 2nd District and Tennessee's 9th District and districts where voters backed Trump in 2024 by more than 10 points like Kentucky's 6th District and Arkansas' 2nd District.
In all, the 70 races that have at least six figures of ad spending from each party voted for Trump by an average of 9 points in 2024.
body_zh: 这些是 11 月 3 日举行的 2026 年中期选举中值得关注的众议院竞选
2026 年 10 月 14 日，爱荷华州得梅因，一名工人在提前投票期间举着“我今天投票”贴纸。查理·尼伯格/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
在 2026 年中期选举的最后一周，广告支出数据表明，核心之争不再是阻止众议院的民主党浪潮，而是弄清楚民主党浪潮能达到多高。
NPR 的一项分析发现，众议院最终的竞争格局非常广阔，包括 70 个选区，双方在每个选区的最后几天的信息传递中投入了至少六位数的资金。
其中包括密歇根州、北卡罗来纳州、纽约州和佛罗里达州各地区的拨款超过 1000 万美元；在田纳西州、俄克拉荷马州和阿肯色州的深红色社区购买了七位数的广告，并向共和党人不公正划分选区可能适得其反的地区提供最后一刻的资源。
在阿肯色州，民主党人在竞争激烈的中期选举地图边缘看到了一个空缺
在不利于执政党的中期环境中，共和党在众议院以 218 比 214 的微弱席位优势似乎几乎肯定会让位于民主党的控制权。库克政治报告的最新评级显示，民主党在 220 个席位中受到青睐，其中 17 个席位被列为“悬而未决”的席位，另外 30 个席位具有潜在竞争力，但倾向于共和党。
在2024年总统选举周期中，多数席位的微弱优势已经改变了民主党的立场，特别是在投票给一党总统候选人和另一党众议院提名人的10个选区。
其中包括民主党众议员 Adam Gray (CA-13)、Nellie Pou (NJ-09) 和 Marie Gluesenkamp-Perez (WA-03) 以及即将退休的共和党众议员 Don Bacon (NE-02) 所持有的席位。
根据 AdImpact 的数据，最近几周共和党人在这四个选区都大幅削减了广告保留。
最新的 NPR/PBS News/Marist 民意调查显示，民主党在注册选民中拥有 10 个百分点的优势，在一般国会选票上，在可能选民中拥有 8 个百分点的优势。这意味着在考虑候选人质量或外部支出之前，纸面上有更多席位具有竞争力。
生活成本仍然是选民最关心的问题，因为油价上涨、关税和伊朗持续的战争给许多美国人带来了经济困境。与此同时，初选中的反现任倾向加剧了国会宣布退休的人数创历史新高。
最高法院进一步撤销部分投票权法案的决定后，十年中期的一波选区重新划分浪潮进一步扰乱了地图，共和党人改变了边界线，将更多保守派选民纳入民主党众议员马西·卡普图尔 (OH-09)、唐·戴维斯 (NC-01)、索马里人物 (AL-02) 和达伦·索托 (FL-09) 控制的选区。
（加州民主党人对目前由共和党众议员 James Gallagher (CA-01)、David Valadao (CA-22)、Ken Calvert (CA-41)、Darrell Issa (CA-48) 和独立人士 Kevin Kiley (CA-06) 控制的选区也采取了同样的做法。
只有数字和索托位于目前被评为有利于共和党的选区。
混乱的国会初选季以创纪录的离场和失利结束
由于数百万选民已经在中期选举中投票，民主党和共和党认为有数十场比赛值得在最后几个小时进行大量投资，以帮助塑造结果。
其中最昂贵的是：密歇根州第七选区和北卡罗来纳州第一选区——每个选区的计划支出都超过 1200 万美元；佛罗里达州第 14、22 和 25 选区；纽约第17区；爱荷华州的第二和第三选区以及许多其他竞选要么有利于民主党，要么被认为是难以预测的。
其中包括共和党今年重新划定的席位，以最大限度地减少民主党的投票权，例如阿拉巴马州的第二选区和田纳西州的第九选区，以及选民在2024年支持特朗普超过10个百分点的选区，例如肯塔基州的第六选区和阿肯色州的第二选区。
总体而言，2024 年，每党广告支出至少为 6 位数的 70 个竞选中，特朗普的平均支持率为 9 个百分点。

title_en: State ballots let voters decide on abortion, taxes, transgender restrictions
title_zh: 州选票让选民决定堕胎、税收、跨性别限制
summary: Missouri voters could ban abortion - after they just removed a ban two years ago. California voters could tax billionaires 5% of their wealth.
summary_zh: 密苏里州选民两年前刚刚取消了堕胎禁令，他们可以禁止堕胎。加州选民可以向亿万富翁征收其财富 5% 的税。
body_en: State ballots let voters decide on abortion, taxes, transgender restrictions

A scene from early voting in Maryland, where voters can decide whether to allow congressional redistricting. It's one of more than 140 state ballot questions around the country this election. Allison Robbert/AP hide caption
Whether or not they live in a competitive congressional district, voters in many states will be deciding on statewide ballot measures with a chance to make law themselves.
There are 145 statewide ballot measures on the November ballot, according to Ballotpedia, which tracks elections.

In some cases the questions were put on the ballot with petition drives by citizens frustrated with the actions - or lack of action - by their state lawmakers. In many cases, legislatures go to the voters with amendments to their state constitution.
There are common themes across the country: many of the most high profile referenda are on abortion, LGBTQ+ rights, taxes, and voting.
Four years after Dobbs, states are still going back and forth on abortion

Four states have abortion on the ballot. That comes after a flurry of ballot measures on the issue since federal protections for the procedure from Roe v. Wade were overturned by the Dobbs decision in 2022.
Some states will ask voters to make it harder to pass constitutional amendments

Just two years ago, Missouri voters nullified what had been one of the strictest abortion bans in the country. But the Republican-led legislature has put the question back on the ballot. And lawmakers crafted a single question that includes both a near-total ban on abortion and prohibitions on gender-affirming medical treatments for minors.
Much of the advertising for the measure just mentions the gender-affirming care ban , which would go into the state constitution to strengthen bans already in state law.
Abortion is legal in Nevada and Virginia but voters in both states will have a chance to put those rights in the state constitution. That would make it harder for future legislatures to ban abortion.
A vote in Idaho could overturn that state's near-total ban on abortion.
States consider transgender restrictions or guaranteeing LGBTQ+ rights
Rights for LGBTQ+ people have been hotly contested in the states in recent years. Several states have them on the ballot.
In Vermont a proposal would amend the state constitution to include an equal protection clause that would guarantee rights for gender identity and gender expression.

Virginia voters could strengthen laws allowing same-sex marriage. The state currently has an old ban on same-sex marriage in its constitution - although it is not in force due to a 2015 US Supreme Court decision. Voters are deciding whether to replace that language through an amendment that would define marriage as between any two adults regardless of race, sex, or gender.
Arizona and Colorado have proposals to ban transgender students in girls school and college sports, with Arizona expanding a current ban by including restrictions on locker rooms and other areas.

A proposal in Washington state would require that a student wanting to play girls sports have their biological sex confirmed by their healthcare provider based on, "the student's reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup, or normal endogenously produced testosterone levels."

In California, Prop. 40 asks voters to impose a wealth tax on billionaires to pay for healthcare programs and two other propositions would block the tax. Opponents say it would chase billionaires out of the state, costing the state money in the long run. Jae C. Hong/AP hide caption
body_zh: 州选票让选民决定堕胎、税收、跨性别限制
马里兰州提前投票的场景，选民可以决定是否允许国会重新划分选区。这是本次选举全国 140 多个州选票问题之一。艾莉森·罗伯特/美联社隐藏标题栏
无论他们是否生活在竞争激烈的国会选区，许多州的选民都将决定全州范围内的投票措施，并有机会自己制定法律。
根据追踪选举的 Ballotpedia 的数据，11 月的投票中有 145 项全州范围的投票措施。
在某些情况下，这些问题是通过对州立法者的行动或缺乏行动感到沮丧的公民发起请愿活动而进行投票的。在许多情况下，立法机关会向选民提出州宪法修正案。
全国各地都有共同的主题：许多最引人注目的公投都是关于堕胎、LGBTQ+ 权利、税收和投票。
多布斯案四年后，各州仍在堕胎问题上摇摆不定
四个州的选票上有堕胎。自 2022 年多布斯案裁决推翻联邦对罗伊诉韦德案程序的保护以来，针对这一问题采取了一系列投票措施。
一些州将要求选民加大宪法修正案通过的难度
就在两年前，密苏里州选民废除了该国最严格的堕胎禁令之一。但共和党领导的立法机构已将这个问题重新放到选票上。立法者提出了一个问题，其中包括几乎完全禁止堕胎和禁止对未成年人进行性别肯定的医疗治疗。
该措施的大部分广告只是提到性别肯定护理禁令，该禁令将写入州宪法，以加强州法律中已有的禁令。
堕胎在内华达州和弗吉尼亚州是合法的，但这两个州的选民将有机会将这些权利写入州宪法。这将使未来的立法机构更难禁止堕胎。
爱达荷州的投票可能会推翻该州近乎全面的堕胎禁令。
各国考虑限制变性人或保障 LGBTQ+ 权利
近年来，LGBTQ+ 人群的权利在各州引起了激烈的争论。有几个州将他们列入选票。
佛蒙特州的一项提案将修改州宪法，纳入平等保护条款，保障性别认同和性别表达的权利。
弗吉尼亚州选民可以加强允许同性婚姻的法律。该州目前宪法中已有一项禁止同性婚姻的旧禁令，但由于 2015 年美国最高法院的裁决，该禁令并未生效。选民正在决定是否通过一项修正案来取代这种语言，该修正案将婚姻定义为任何两个成年人之间的婚姻，无论种族、性别或性别。
亚利桑那州和科罗拉多州已提议禁止变性学生参加女子学校和大学体育运动，亚利桑那州扩大了当前的禁令，包括对更衣室和其他区域的限制。
华盛顿州的一项提案要求，想要参加女子运动的学生必须由医疗保健提供者根据“学生的生殖解剖结构、基因构成或正常的内源性睾酮水平”确认其生物性别。
在加利福尼亚州，第 40 号提案要求选民对亿万富翁征收财富税，以支付医疗保健计划的费用，另外两项提案将阻止征收该税。反对者表示，这会将亿万富翁赶出该州，从长远来看会花费该州的钱。 Jae C. Hong/美联社隐藏标题栏

title_en: Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal
title_zh: 民意调查显示，白人福音派人士对特朗普的支持率大幅下降
summary: Three new polls suggest that President Trump is losing ground among white evangelicals. What explains this drop — and will it affect the midterm elections?
summary_zh: 三项新民意调查显示，特朗普总统在白人福音派中正在失去支持率。是什么解释了这种下降——它会影响中期选举吗
body_en: Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal : NPR

Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal Three new polls suggest that President Trump is losing ground among white evangelicals. What explains this drop — and will it affect the midterm elections?
Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal
Three new polls suggest that President Trump is losing ground among white evangelicals. What explains this drop — and will it affect the midterm elections?

White evangelicals are usually President Trump's most loyal backers. New polling shows their support for Trump has plummeted. Jack Jenkins of Religion News Service talked to evangelicals about what's behind the shift.

JACK JENKINS, BYLINE: Pastor Robert Jeffress is best known for two things - serving as pastor of First Baptist Church in Dallas, Texas, and being one of the most vocal evangelical supporters of President Trump. But while Jeffress remains bullish on Trump, he's concerned about how factors like prices at the pump are pulling the president's approval rating down.
ROBERT JEFFRESS: You know, evangelicals have to fill up their tanks with gasoline as well.
KRISTIN DU MEZ: Yeah. This is probably one of the very few times I'll go on record agreeing with Robert Jeffress.
JENKINS: That's Kristin Du Mez, a historian who studies evangelicalism at Calvin University.

DU MEZ: Inasmuch as there is a decline in evangelical support for Trump, I would interpret it in terms of the economy, in terms of, you know, these general trends that we're seeing across nearly every demographic.

JENKINS: Since 2016, white evangelicals have formed the most loyal part of Trump's base. Around 8 in 10 approved of his actions in the White House as of early last year. But the number has been dropping precipitously in recent weeks. Now three polls all show double-digit declines in his support among white evangelicals. According to a Pew Research Center poll released earlier this month, Trump's approval rating has dropped 20 points from 78% to 58%.
RALPH REED: We're hearing what you would expect to hear, which is concerns about cost of living, concerns about gas prices.

JENKINS: That's Ralph Reed, a longtime evangelical activist and political consultant known as one of the architects of the religious right. And there may be other factors beyond dollars and cents here. Michael Weir is a Democrat and an evangelical organizer who helped former President Obama court religious voters. He says Trump's drop in support among conservative Christians may signal a bit of evangelical exhaustion with the president.

MICHAEL WEIR: I don't think we're going to see massive, massive swings of conservative evangelicals voting for Democrats, but there is a bit of buyer's remorse, a bit of this is not what we signed up for, a bit of just weariness with it all.
JENKINS: Du Mez says some evangelicals are trying to rally their faithful back to Trump and Republicans despite the economic woes.

DU MEZ: That is rhetoric that I am hearing from conservative evangelicals. Yes, these gas prices are wild right now. But if we are ensuring a safe country for our children, it is all worth it. We are willing to pay the price.

JENKINS: The fact that this drop in Trump support has happened on the eve of the congressional midterms makes some conservative activists nervous. Ralph Reed is working hard to combat it. At a Trump rally in Dalton, Georgia, he planned to recruit volunteers to help turn out evangelical voters in the midterm elections. He's peppering evangelical voters with messages that tap into longstanding concerns, namely Democrats' more liberal positions on issues such as Israel, LGBTQ rights and abortion.
REED: You get into the pro-life issues and the gender issues. And all that is on our voter guides that are going into churches. It's on all the door hangers.

JENKINS: In the past, Trump's support among evangelicals has dipped and then recovered. But it has never dropped this far, this close to an election. And now the key question is whether this downward trend will continue.
body_zh: 民意调查显示，白人福音派人士对特朗普的支持率大幅下降：NPR
民调显示，白人福音派人士对特朗普的支持率大幅下降 三项新民意调查显示，特朗普总统在白人福音派人士中的支持率正在下降。如何解释这种下降——它会影响中期选举吗？
民意调查显示，白人福音派人士对特朗普的支持率大幅下降
三项新民意调查显示，特朗普总统在白人福音派中正在失去支持率。如何解释这种下降——它会影响中期选举吗？
白人福音派人士通常是特朗普总统最忠实的支持者。新的民意调查显示，他们对特朗普的支持率大幅下降。宗教新闻社的杰克·詹金斯与福音派人士谈论了这一转变背后的原因。
杰克·詹金斯连线：罗伯特·杰弗里斯牧师因两件事而闻名——担任德克萨斯州达拉斯第一浸信会教堂的牧师，以及是特朗普总统最直言不讳的福音派支持者之一。不过，尽管杰弗里斯仍然看好特朗普，但他担心加油站价格等因素会如何拉低总统的支持率。
罗伯特·杰弗里斯：你知道，福音派也必须给他们的油箱加满汽油。
克里斯汀·杜梅斯：是的。这可能是我极少数公开同意罗伯特·杰弗里斯观点的一次。
詹金斯：这是克里斯汀·杜梅斯，一位在加尔文大学研究福音派的历史学家。
杜梅兹：由于福音派对特朗普的支持有所下降，我会从经济角度来解释它，你知道，我们在几乎每个人口中都看到了这些总体趋势。
詹金斯：自 2016 年以来，白人福音派人士已成为特朗普基地最忠诚的部分。截至去年初，大约十分之八的人认可他在白宫的行动。但最近几周这个数字急剧下降。现在三项民意调查均显示他在白人福音派中的支持率出现了两位数的下降。皮尤研究中心本月早些时候公布的民意调查显示，特朗普的支持率下降了20个百分点，从78%降至58%。
拉尔夫·里德：我们听到的是您所期望听到的，即对生活成本的担忧，对汽油价格的担忧。
詹金斯：那是拉尔夫·里德，一位长期的福音派活动家和政治顾问，被称为宗教右翼的缔造者之一。除了金钱之外，可能还有其他因素。迈克尔·威尔是一名民主党人和福音派组织者，帮助前总统奥巴马赢得宗教选民的支持。他说，特朗普在保守派基督徒中的支持​​率下降可能表明总统对福音派有些疲惫。
迈克尔·威尔：我认为我们不会看到保守派福音派人士投票支持民主党的大规模摇摆，但买家有一点悔恨，这并不是我们所希望的，只是对这一切感到厌倦。
詹金斯：杜梅兹说，尽管经济困难，一些福音派人士仍试图将他们的信徒重新团结起来支持特朗普和共和党。
DU MEZ：这是我从保守福音派那里听到的言论。是的，现在汽油价格太高了。但如果我们能够确保我们的孩子有一个安全的国家，那么一切都是值得的。我们愿意付出代价。
詹金斯：特朗普支持率的下降发生在国会中期选举前夕，这一事实让一些保守派活动人士感到紧张。拉尔夫·里德正在努力与之抗争。在佐治亚州道尔顿举行的特朗普集会上，他计划招募志愿者，帮助在中期选举中选出福音派选民。他向福音派选民传达了一些信息，这些信息涉及长期关注的问题，即民主党在以色列、LGBTQ 权利和堕胎等问题上更加自由的立场。
里德：你谈到了反堕胎问题和性别问题。所有这些都在我们即将进入教堂的选民指南中。所有门衣架上都有它。
詹金斯：过去，特朗普在福音派中的支持率先下降后恢复。但它从未下降如此之远，如此接近选举。现在的关键问题是这种下降趋势是否会持续下去。

body_en: Hegseth reportedly fires high-ranking army strategist over alleged leaks | US military
Hegseth reportedly fires high-ranking army strategist over alleged leaks
Pentagon says it has referred leak case to justice department for criminal investigation

The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , has reportedly dismissed Lt Gen Brett Sylvia, a high-ranking army strategist serving on the Pentagon’s joint staff, following allegations that he disclosed classified information to the public.

The Pentagon announced on Thursday that it had referred an alleged information leak case for criminal investigation, maintaining that the removal of the senior general was essential “to protect sensitive information”, the Washington Post reported.
Sylvia had served as the director for strategy, plans and policy on the joint staff.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell acknowledged the dismissal in a statement on social media, though he did not mention Sylvia by name.
Democratic senator says Hegseth trying to hide costs of Iran war from US public

“Following an extensive Air Force OSI investigation, the Department took necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information,” Parnell wrote. “To protect the integrity of the investigation, no further comment will be made regarding the individual or the circumstances of this action.”
“This matter, along with others, have been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action,” he added.
A spokesperson for the Department of Justice said in a statement that it “has ongoing investigations related to possible leaks of classified information”.
“We work closely with our government partners, which includes the Department of War,” the spokesperson added, using the Trump administration’s name for the Pentagon.

Sylvia’s removal represents one of the most significant actions so far in Hegseth’s extensive campaign to identify officials suspected of sharing information with journalists, as the unpopular US war on Iran moves into its ninth month.

In July, Hegseth ​announced that the Pentagon and the US Department of Justice had created a joint taskforce “​to identify and ​prosecute” what he called the “unauthorized disclosure ​of sensitive” information to the press.
Last year, Hegseth implemented new restrictions governing media access that prompted legal concerns from press organizations.
Dozens of journalists surrendered their press badges rather than agree to the new media policies, which have been subject to legal challenges.
A senior Pentagon official told Reuters that Sylvia failed three separate polygraph tests, in which he was asked whether he had disclosed classified material.

“The extent of his leaking became so critical that Secretary Hegseth took immediate action and fired Sylvia in order to protect national security. Urgent action was needed and could not wait another second,” the official said, according to Reuters.

However, a colleague of Sylvia told the Washington Post that the general had consistently rejected accusations that he leaked classified information, while also acknowledging that he had previously communicated with members of the press.

In August, three journalists fired by the Pentagon from the US government-funded news outlet Stars and Stripes sued the department in federal court, arguing their dismissals were illegal and violated their first amendment rights to free speech.
body_zh: 据报道，赫格斯因涉嫌泄密而解雇了高级陆军战略家美军
据报道，赫格斯因涉嫌泄密而解雇了高级陆军战略家
五角大楼表示已将泄密案件移交司法部进行刑事调查
据报道，美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 解雇了五角大楼联合参谋部高级陆军战略家布雷特·西尔维娅 (Brett Sylvia) 中将，原因是他被指控向公众披露机密信息。
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，五角大楼周四宣布，已将涉嫌信息泄露的案件移交刑事调查，并坚称解除这位高级将军的职务对于“保护敏感信息”至关重要。
西尔维娅曾担任联合参谋部战略、计划和政策总监。
五角大楼发言人肖恩·帕内尔在社交媒体上的一份声明中承认了这一解雇，但他没有提到西尔维娅的名字。
民主党参议员称赫格斯试图向美国公众隐瞒伊朗战争的代价
帕内尔写道：“在进行广泛的空军现场视察调查后，国防部采取了必要的人事行动来保护敏感信息。” “为了保护调查的完整性，不会对此次行动的个人或情况发表进一步评论。”
他补充说：“这件事以及其他问题已被提交给司法部，以便采取进一步的法律行动。”
司法部发言人在一份声明中表示，“正在对可能泄露的机密信息进行调查”。
“我们与包括陆军部在内的政府合作伙伴密切合作，”发言人补充道，并使用了特朗普政府对五角大楼的名称。
随着不受欢迎的美国对伊朗战争进入第九个月，西尔维娅的免职是赫格塞斯为查明涉嫌与记者分享信息的官员而开展的广泛行动中迄今为止最重要的行动之一。
7 月，赫格斯宣布五角大楼和美国司法部成立了一个联合工作组，“识别并起诉”他所谓的向媒体“未经授权披露敏感”信息的行为。
去年，赫格斯实施了新的媒体访问限制，引发了新闻机构的法律担忧。
数十名记者放弃了记者证，而不是同意新媒体政策，这些政策一直受到法律挑战。
一名五角大楼高级官员告诉路透社，西尔维娅未能通过三项单独的测谎仪测试，测试中他被问及是否披露了机密材料。
据路透社报道，该官员表示：“他泄密的程度变得如此严重，以至于赫格斯部长为了保护国家安全立即采取了行动并解雇了西尔维娅。需要采取紧急行动，不能再等了。”
然而，西尔维娅的一位同事告诉《华盛顿邮报》，这位将军一直否认有关他泄露机密信息的指控，同时也承认他之前曾与新闻界人士进行过沟通。
8月，五角大楼解雇了美国政府资助的新闻媒体《星条旗报》的三名记者，他们在联邦法院起诉五角大楼，称解雇他们是非法的，并侵犯了他们言论自由的第一修正案权利。

body_en: DHS cites risk to more than 40,000 personnel in effort to take leaked data offline | Trump administration
DHS cites risk to more than 40,000 personnel in effort to take leaked data offline
The Department of Homeland Security asked an Icelandic hosting company to take down data obtained through hack

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) asked ⁠an Icelandic hosting company on Thursday to take down or limit access to data related to thousands ⁠of agency personnel, saying ⁠the content ​put them at risk, according to the request posted online by hosting company FlokiNET.
The database “places more than ⁠40,000 identifiable individuals at risk of harassment, stalking and physical harm”, the request said.
ZeroFox, a company authorized by the US ⁠ Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency to pursue content removal actions, cited the figure in ​an email to FlokiNET.
Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers

FlokiNET’s ‌CEO, Kolja Weber, told ‌Reuters that his company would not remove the DHS data because it ‌included government employee work addresses and work phone numbers, not personal phone numbers and addresses.

A DHS spokesperson said the agency “is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively. We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously ‌and will work to ensure all are properly protected.”

The non-profit data transparency group DDoSecrets released data on more than 40,000 DHS personnel ​on its website on Wednesday, alongside a separate, searchable database developed by hacker and journalist “maia arson crimew”. The database was briefly inaccessible on Thursday but was soon republished at a different domain.

A group calling itself “the Department of Peace” claimed responsibility ⁠for obtaining the data, and said in a statement on Wednesday ​that DHS ​employees “have our information, so it’s only ​fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped ​the data “can be ‌used to limit ​further harm ​by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”.
Privacy advocates have criticized the DHS’s use of personal data from other agencies, including Medicaid records and taxpayer data, for immigration enforcement.

国土安全部称，为了将泄露的数据下线，超过 40,000 名人员面临风险
美国国土安全部要求一家冰岛托管公司删除通过黑客获取的数据
根据托管公司 FlokiNET 在网上发布的请求，美国国土安全部 (DHS) 周四要求一家冰岛托管公司删除或限制访问与数千名机构人员相关的数据，称这些内容将他们置于危险之中。
请求称，该数据库“使超过 40,000 名可识别的个人面临骚扰、跟踪和人身伤害的风险”。
ZeroFox 是一家获得美国移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 机构授权采取内容删除行动的公司，在发给 FlokiNET 的电子邮件中引用了这一数字。
非营利组织泄露 40,000 多名国土安全人员的数据
FlokiNET 的首席执行官 Kolja Weber 告诉路透社，他的公司不会删除国土安全部的数据，因为其中包括政府雇员的工作地址和工作电话号码，而不是个人电话号码和地址。
国土安全部发言人表示，该机构“意识到潜在的违规行为，正在积极努力迅速有效地解决这一问题。我们认真对待针对员工和官员的所有安全威胁，并将努力确保所有人都得到适当的保护。”
非营利性数据透明组织 DDoSecrets 周三在其网站上发布了超过 40,000 名国土安全部人员的数据，以及由黑客和记者“maia arsoncrimew”开发的独立的可搜索数据库。该数据库在周四短暂无法访问，但很快就在不同的域上重新发布。
一个自称“和平部”的组织声称对获取这些数据负责，并在周三的一份声明中表示，国土安全部员工“拥有我们的信息，因此我们拥有他们的信息是公平的”，并希望这些数据“可用于限制国土安全部的进一步伤害，并支持朝这个方向的所有努力”。
隐私倡导者批评国土安全部使用其他机构的个人数据（包括医疗补助记录和纳税人数据）来执行移民执法。

body_en: Alaska's tight Senate race is facing a new controversy over two candidates named Dan Sullivan appearing on the ballot — a twist that's drawn attention from President Trump .
The big picture: The controversy is adding uncertainty to one of the nation's most competitive Senate contests, with control of Congress on the line in next week's midterm elections.

Catch up quick: The New York Times reported this week that Democratic operatives with ties to Mary Peltola's Senate campaign helped recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan to challenge Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan.
Trump accused Peltola and Democrats of election fraud and called for criminal prosecution, though the Times did not establish that any laws were broken.
Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into Peltola's campaign over the NYT report. House Republicans are also launching an Alaska Senate race probe.
Though the presence of two Sullivans in the Senate race has been known for months, the Times' report adds a new wrinkle to a dispute that's already reached the courts.
The controversy centers on two candidates with nearly identical names appearing on Alaska's Senate ballot: Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan and unaffiliated challenger Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
The ballot will show registered Republican "Sullivan, Dan S." and unaffiliated candidate "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr." Peltola and Republican Gerald Heikes will also be on the ballot.
The challenger initially filed as a Republican but later changed his registration to undeclared. He will appear on the ballot without a party label.
Flashback: Concerns about the duplicate names have existed for months.
In June, a top Alaskan election official ruled that candidate Daniel J. Sullivan was ineligible to run on the state's primary ballot.
The official said she found the candidacy was "filed with a purpose to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the ballot's fairness or neutrality," per the Associated Press.
The Alaska Supreme Court later ruled that state election officials lacked the authority to disqualify Sullivan based on their concerns about his motives, allowing him to appear on the ballot.
The court did not determine whether his candidacy was intended to mislead voters.

Flashback: Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska, seeking to block certification of the Senate election if the incumbent loses by a margin potentially attributable to voters confusing the two Sullivans.
Both Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee have asked a federal judge to dismiss the case.
Alaska officials are seeking dismissal of the lawsuit, arguing that it has no legal basis and that the federal government lacks authority to intervene in a matter governed by state election law.

Zoom in: The new NYT report , published this week, cited texts, interviews and documents showing that Peltola's aides worked with Democratic operatives to recruit candidates who could siphon votes from the Republican senator.
Per the report, a staffer was told to review every "Dan Sullivan" in the state, leading the team to Dan J. Sullivan, the retired schoolteacher who was registered as a Republican.
Peltola's campaign and the DSCC denied recruiting Sullivan, per NYT.

总体情况：这场争议给美国竞争最激烈的参议院竞选之一增添了不确定性，下周的中期选举中国会的控制权岌岌可危。
赶上：《纽约时报》本周报道称，与玛丽·佩尔托拉（ Mary Peltola ）参议院竞选活动有联系的民主党特工帮助招募了一名名叫丹· J ·沙利文（ Dan J. Sullivan ）的候选人，以挑战共和党现任总统丹· S ·沙
特朗普指责佩尔托拉和民主党选举舞弊，并呼吁进行刑事起诉，尽管《泰晤士报》并未证实他们违反了任何法律。
阿拉斯加州州长迈克邓利维因纽约时报的报道下令对佩尔托拉的竞选活动进行调查。众议院共和党人还启动了阿拉斯加参议院种族调查。
尽管两名沙利文参加参议院竞选的消息几个月前就已为人所知，但《泰晤士报》的报道为已经提交法院的争议增添了新的麻烦。
争议集中在阿拉斯加参议院投票中出现的两名姓名几乎相同的候选人：共和党现任议员丹·S·沙利文和无党派挑战者小丹尼尔·J·沙利文。
选票将显示注册共和党人“Sullivan, Dan S.”和无党派候选人“Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.“佩尔托拉和共和党人杰拉尔德·海克斯也将参加投票。
挑战者最初以共和党身份提交申请，但后来将其注册改为未申报。他将出现在没有政党标签的选票上。
闪回：对重复名称的担忧已经存在了几个月。
六月，阿拉斯加一位高级选举官员裁定候选人丹尼尔·J·沙利文没有资格参加该州的初选。
据美联社报道，这位官员表示，她发现候选人资格“提交的目的是为了混淆或误导，从而损害选票的公平性或中立性”。
阿拉斯加州最高法院后来裁定，州选举官员无权基于对沙利文动机的担忧而取消他的资格，允许他出现在选票上。
法院没有确定他的候选资格是否旨在误导选民。
回顾：上周，司法部起诉阿拉斯加州，如果现任者因选民混淆了两个沙利文而以微弱优势落败，则寻求阻止参议院选举的认证。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队和民主党参议员竞选委员会都要求联邦法官驳回此案。
阿拉斯加官员正在寻求驳回该诉讼，认为该诉讼没有法律依据，而且联邦政府无权干预受州选举法管辖的事项。
放大：本周发布的《纽约时报》新报道引用了文本、采访和文件，显示佩尔托拉的助手与民主党工作人员合作，招募可以从共和党参议员那里窃取选票的候选人。
根据该报告，一名工作人员被告知要审查该州的每一位“丹·沙利文”，并带领团队找到了注册为共和党人的退休教师丹·J·沙利文。
据《纽约时报》报道，佩尔托拉的竞选团队和 DSCC 否认招募沙利文。
